about.title: About TechPulse
sections: Purpose
TechPulse is a technology and gaming intelligence platform designed to help readers discover important developments, understand why they matter, and navigate to original reporting.
How it works
TechPulse collects configured RSS/Atom feeds, normalizes and validates items, removes duplicates, categorizes stories and calculates prioritization signals before publishing a static dataset.
What TechPulse provides
TechPulse provides original summaries, source attribution, ranking signals, daily briefings, story intelligence and links to original publishers.
What TechPulse does not claim
A TP Score, confidence value or status label is not a guarantee that a claim has been independently fact-checked.
Editorial independence
Ranking and presentation should not be altered to favor a publisher, advertiser, sponsor or commercial interest.

editorial.title: Editorial Policy
sections: Accuracy
TechPulse prioritizes accurate attribution, clear timestamps, source identity and separation between reported facts, analysis, forecasts and developing information.
Source selection
Sources are selected for relevance, reporting quality, expertise, freshness, feed reliability and usefulness.
Original summaries
TechPulse summaries are independently worded and intended to help readers understand why a report matters. TechPulse does not intentionally reproduce complete third-party articles.
Ranking
Stories are prioritized using importance, confidence, freshness, momentum and source-quality signals. Ranking is a navigation aid, not a statement of truth.
Developing stories
Information that is incomplete, changing or insufficiently corroborated should be presented with appropriate uncertainty.
Corrections
Known material errors should be corrected promptly.
Automation
Automated collection and scoring are used for scale and consistency and are not represented as human fact-checking.

copyright.title: Copyright & Content Policy
sections: Third-party rights
Copyright in original articles, trademarks, logos, photographs and other publisher materials remains with their respective rights holders.
TechPulse summaries
TechPulse aims to publish concise, independently worded summaries rather than reproduce complete third-party articles.
Publisher links
External links direct readers to original reporting. Availability and licensing conditions are controlled by the respective publisher.
Rights concerns
Rights holders should use the designated TechPulse contact channel for copyright or content concerns.

source.title: Source Policy
sections: Source quality
Source quality is a prioritization signal based on configured source metadata and observed feed characteristics; it is not a universal rating of a publisher.
Source transparency
Where available, TechPulse displays publisher, source type, publication time and original article link.
Corroboration
Multiple reports may strengthen context but do not automatically prove a claim true.
Feed failures
A failed feed should not erase the last valid dataset. The collector should retain known-good data and retry failed sources.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
sections: Core experience
The GitHub Pages edition does not require an account. Saved stories and interface preferences are stored locally in the browser.
Local storage
The site may store saved story IDs, language, theme, font size and reduced-motion preference in browser local storage.
External publishers
When a reader opens an original article, the browser connects directly to the external publisher and that publisher's privacy practices apply.
Future services
If analytics, accounts, subscriptions, advertising or server-side AI are introduced, this policy should be updated before those services are enabled.

terms.title: Terms of Use
sections: Informational service
TechPulse is provided for general information and discovery. It is not professional, legal, financial, medical, investment or security advice.
External content
TechPulse links to third-party publishers and does not control external availability, accuracy, licensing or editorial decisions.
No guarantee
Reasonable engineering controls are used, but no online service can guarantee uninterrupted availability, complete accuracy or immunity from attack.
Acceptable use
Users must not intentionally abuse the service, bypass security controls, distribute malicious traffic, scrape at harmful rates or interfere with availability.

corrections.title: Corrections Policy
sections: What qualifies
Corrections may be required for materially inaccurate summaries, incorrect attribution, wrong timestamps, misleading status labels or other significant errors.
How corrections are handled
A correction may update, reclassify, suppress or remove affected information.
Reporting
Production deployment should provide a monitored correction channel.

contact.title: Contact & Security Reporting
sections: Production contact
Before public launch, replace the contact placeholder with a monitored company-owned email address or support portal.
Security reports
Security vulnerabilities should be reported privately through the designated security contact rather than posted publicly.

methodology.title: TP Score Methodology
sections: Definition
TP Score is a 0–100 prioritization score designed to help readers identify stories that deserve attention.
Components
Importance 30%; Confidence 25%; Freshness 20%; Momentum 15%; Source Quality 10%.
Interpretation
85–100: High Impact. 70–84: Significant. 50–69: Watch. Below 50: Low Signal.
Limitation
TP Score is not a truth score, fact-check score or guarantee of independent verification.
